claims.text: An ECG is nearly always done but doesn't diagnose dissection: findings range from normal to markedly abnormal.
claims.quote: Electrocardiography (ECG) is nearly universally done. However, findings range from normal to markedly abnormal (in acute coronary artery occlusion or aortic regurgitation), so the test is not diagnostically helpful for dissection itself.

claims.text: Inferior MI changes plus a new aortic regurgitation murmur raise concern for a type I dissection into the right coronary artery.
claims.quote: Patients presenting with acute chest pain, electrocardiography (ECG) changes of acute inferior myocardial infarction, and a previously undocumented murmur of aortic regurgitation (AR) are of particular concern for a type I aortic dissection into the right coronary artery
